$comment: The shape of a real `act --json` log line, as the extractors in src/evidence assume it.
This file is an ASSERTION ABOUT A THIRD-PARTY TOOL, and it says so per field.
`scripts/smoke-real-act.sh` reads it, computes the same facts from a log captured from a
live act, and prints the difference (docs/testing.md §7). A field marked
"assumed_by": [...] that a real run never emits is a contract gap, not a cosmetic one:
it means a record this server publishes is being computed from something that is not there.
PROVENANCE — how each row was established, and how strong the claim is:
source  = read out of nektos/act at the tag named in `note`, which is a strong claim
about that version but still not a capture.
capture = seen in a log produced by a real run and committed to this directory.
Every row below is `source`. Nothing here has been captured yet: no machine running this
repository's CI had both act and a container runtime when this file was written, and a
golden fabricated from an assumption is worse than no golden. Run
`scripts/smoke-real-act.sh --capture-golden` on a box that has them and commit what it
writes; `golden/README.md` is the policy.
logrus, not act, writes the three base fields: act sets `logrus.JSONFormatter` for
--json (cmd/root.go newRunCommand, pkg/runner/logger.go WithJobLogger), and that
formatter emits `level`, `msg`, `time` (RFC 3339, whole seconds) plus every entry field,
marshalled with encoding/json — which is why a Go time.Duration is an INTEGER (ns) and
not the '1m28.234s' its String() prints.

provenance.supported_range_of_this_server: 0.2.62 ..= 0.2.97 (src/workspace.rs MINIMUM_ACT_VERSION and the range ADR-0003 §1.3 names)
provenance.method: source inspection of the released tags; one live non-job line from act v0.2.63 (see observed_first_line)

observed_first_line.comment: A real act v0.2.63 run in a sandbox with no container runtime. It is act's own JSON output, and it carries none of the job fields — which is why no field outside base_fields may be treated as present on every line.

line.msg: Couldn't get a valid docker connection: no DOCKER_HOST and an invalid container socket ''

assumed_by: src/evidence/benchmark/act_log.rs (ignored, but every line has it)
src/evidence/benchmark/act_log.rs (the in-band ACTMCP_BENCHMARK marker rides in here)
msg.note: A step's stdout arrives here one line per entry, on the lines that also carry raw_output:true (pkg/runner/run_context.go rawLogger).

assumed_by: src/evidence/benchmark/act_log.rs (the log span, and step timing attribution)
time.note: logrus default JSON timestamp: RFC3339, so no fractional seconds.

job.required_within: any line that carries a job
job.note: The job's `name:` (or its id when it has no name). Set by WithJobLogger on every job-scoped line: lines act logs outside a job (the docker-connection warning above) carry neither job nor jobID.

jobID.required_within: any line that carries a job
assumed_by: src/evidence/benchmark/act_log.rs attribution() — this is the key a run is matched on
jobID.note: The `jobs:` key. WithJobLogger sets job and jobID together.

dryrun.note: WithJobLogger. Always false for a real run; the fixtures spell it false.

matrix.note: WithJobLogger. A matrix expansion's variables, or null. Not in the fixtures: a field the extractors must ignore rather than trip over.

assumed_by: src/evidence/benchmark/act_log.rs (the step label on a step_duration_s record)

stepID.note: withStepLogger writes []string — an ARRAY, even for the single id a plain run step has, and a composite action's steps append to it. The fixtures spell it ["1"] and that is correct, which is worth saying because an array is an unusual shape for this field's name.

assumed_by: src/evidence/benchmark/act_log.rs (documented; step timings are not filtered by stage)
stage.note: withStepLogger. Note the *message* uses the display spelling ('Main'), the field uses the lowercase one.

assumed_by: src/evidence/benchmark/act_log.rs (documented as the verdict beside executionTime)
stepResult.note: pkg/runner/step.go: the Success/Failure line is the same line that carries executionTime.

jobResult.note: pkg/runner/job_executor.go, on the '🏁  Job succeeded' line — two spaces after the emoji, as in msg.

raw_output.required_within: the lines carrying a step's own stdout/stderr
raw_output.note: run_context.go / action.go / step_docker.go set rawLogger = WithField("raw_output", true). This is the field the whole in-band marker channel depends on, and ADR-0003 V2 asks whether --quiet=false keeps these lines: if a real run's log has no raw_output lines, the marker channel is dead.

assumed_by: src/evidence/benchmark/act_log.rs — step_duration_s and job_duration_s are built from THIS FIELD AND NOTHING ELSE
executionTime.note: THE FIELD TO WATCH. It does not exist in every act in the supported range: pkg/runner/step.go gained it between v0.2.75 and v0.2.76 (absent at v0.2.62..=0.2.75, present through v0.2.97). On an older act the extractor finds no timings at all and now says so — the run carries the named warning act_step_timings_unavailable instead of publishing a silent zero; see known_gaps and docs/benchmark-inputs.md §3.

assumed_by: src/evidence/benchmark/act_log.rs messages() reads msg, Output and Error
Output.note: NOT ACT'S. No tag in the supported range emits `Output` or `Error` as log fields; the fallback in messages() came from a fixture, not from act. Harmless today (the read is a fallback behind msg), listed here so that the smoke's 'fields no one claimed' and 'fields we claimed that never appear' reports stay honest.

command.note: v0.2.97 pkg/runner/command.go / step.go: a workflow runner command (::set-env::, ::error::, a job summary) is logged as structured fields — command, name, arg, kvPairs, raw, content. A step that prints ::group:: lines therefore adds fields no fixture has ever shown. Extractors ignore unknown fields, and the smoke lists these under 'observed and unclaimed' rather than failing on them.

name.note: See command. (Also: a benchmark marker's own `name` lives inside a marker payload, never at the top level of a log line — a top-level `name` is act's.)

known_gaps.gap: act emits step timings only from v0.2.76. This server's floor is MINIMUM_ACT_VERSION 0.2.62, so on act 0.2.62..=0.2.75 every benchmark record's act_log timings are absent — the run still succeeds and publishes the job's own metrics, and job_duration_s/step_duration_s simply do not appear.
known_gaps.settled_by: source: pkg/runner/step.go at v0.2.75 (absent) and v0.2.76 (present)
known_gaps.decided: mact-s3l: the floor stays 0.2.62 and the case is named, not silent. A run whose step-completion lines carried no executionTime carries the warning act_step_timings_unavailable plus a detail line naming v0.2.76 and what job_duration_s fell back to. Reasoning and operator options: docs/benchmark-inputs.md §3.
known_gaps.what_to_do: Still check it against a live log: a log with stepResult Success/Failure lines and no executionTime on any of them is this gap, and the run must then carry act_step_timings_unavailable (scripts/smoke-real-act.sh checks for exactly that). If a live act >= v0.2.76 ever omits executionTime, that is a NEW divergence and this gap no longer explains it.

known_gaps.gap: messages() reads two fields no released act emits. They are dead code masquerading as compatibility.
known_gaps.settled_by: source across the whole supported range
known_gaps.what_to_do: Delete the fallback or say why it stays. The smoke reports them as claimed-but-never-observed.
